title: TakeSix, explained by itself
description: Click any block to open it. Every screen shows six blocks at most; longer text opens next to the block

blocks.title: The idea
blocks.description: Answers as diagrams you click into, not pages of prose. Click me, more inside
blocks.details: Ask an agent to explain a codebase, a spec or a plan and you usually get many screens of headings and bullet lists. TakeSix turns that answer into a tree: the whole thing fits on the first screen, and each part opens into its own screen.

children.title: Six at most
children.description: A screen you can take in at a glance
children.details: Six is a hard limit, checked by the validator. When there are more things to show, they are grouped into a parent that names what they share. That grouping is the explanation.

children.title: Depth on demand
children.description: The gist first, details one click away
children.details: Cards show a title and one line. Click to open a block, use the breadcrumb to go back. Long explanations, code and lists open in a Markdown popup next to the block.

children.title: Checked, not guessed
children.description: JSON with a schema an agent can check
children.details: Errors come with JSON paths (`/blocks/2/children: 7 blocks on one level`), so the agent fixes its own answer before you see it.

blocks.title: For agents
blocks.details: Both teach the agent the same rules for readable diagrams, check the result and render it.

children.title: Agent Skill
children.description: For Claude: rules, validate and render
children.details: Copy `skill/takesix` from the takesix-agent repository into `~/.claude/skills/`. It needs only Node.js: the script and the viewer are bundled.

children.title: MCP server
children.details:
```
claude mcp add takesix -- npx -y @takesix/mcp
codex mcp add takesix -- npx -y @takesix/mcp
```
Tools: `guide` (the rules), `validate`, `show` (writes one HTML file). Runs locally over stdio.

children.title: In the conversation
children.description: MCP Apps hosts show the diagram inline
children.details: In clients that support MCP Apps, such as Claude Desktop, `show` opens the diagram right in the chat, with a full screen button. Elsewhere you get a self-contained HTML file.

children.title: Block
children.description: id, title, place, up to six children
children.details: Besides `id`, `title` and `at`: `icon`, a one-line `description`, `details` (Markdown that opens next to the block), `children` and `meta` for data of other tools. Ids are stable, so links and comments can rely on them.

children.title: Grid
children.description: 6×6 per level; a block covers e.g. A1:C2

children.title: Link
children.description: Between any two blocks, on any levels
children.details: `from`, `to`, an optional `label` and `direction`. A link between nested blocks also shows one level up, as an arrow between their parents.

children.title: @takesix/react
children.description: One component: view, or edit with onChange
children.details:
```tsx
import { TakeSix } from '@takesix/react'
import '@takesix/react/style.css'

<TakeSix document={doc} onChange={setDoc} editing />
```
Light and dark themes, drag and drop, grouping, phones. This page uses it.

children.title: @takesix/core
children.details: Everything about the document without UI: `parseDocument`, `validateDocument`, immutable edits, and `visibleLinks` for drawing arrows on a level.

blocks.title: Open source
blocks.description: MIT: format, libraries, skill, MCP server

children.title: Repositories
children.description: core, react, agent, and this site
